Your headphones will restart to switch LE Audio on/off. Audio stops for a few seconds and Earshot reconnects by itself. With LE Audio on, some shortcut buttons (such as the voice assistant or a music-service shortcut) and multipoint may not work, and this phone may keep using Classic Bluetooth (AAC/SBC) if it does not support LE Audio for these headphones.

An experiment. On some Samsung phones it leaves more headroom so calls can get louder, but it mostly changes how media volume behaves (you may need to turn up both sides for music) and any in-call effect is up to the phone: absolute volume is a media setting, while call volume travels on the call link (HFP) as its own 0–15 setting. To revert, switch it back here, or in Developer options → “Disable absolute volume”, then reconnect.

No app can process the call microphone: on Android it goes from the headset to the modem or the calling app without passing through other apps, and Earshot can\'t reach a mic EQ on the headset. What does help is a wideband call codec (mSBC or LC3) and LE Audio; if you still sound bad on mSBC or LC3, the limit is the network or the calling app. Sidetone, where the headset offers it (in More), changes only what you hear.

The scanner only reads: it sends the connected headset\'s documented read requests and shows the raw replies, and every request passes that headset\'s own write guard as a read. The Print console below is the one part of Lab that writes.
